Subject: MSA redlines + Private deployment addendum questions

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We've reviewed the MSA and Order Form and have attached a marked-up PDF with our redlines focused on Private deployment specifics. High-level concerns:

- License scope: we need explicit language that allows ACME to run the licensed model on our controlled VPC and within our air-gapped clusters; confirm whether that requires a separate license grant or is covered by the current Order Form.
- Deployment rights: we want the right to run copies for DR/testing in a different region; please indicate any restrictions on number of instances or nodes.
- Audit & evidence: because we are regulated, we require quarterly audit rights (read-only access to logs) or an attestation from Redwood. We are open to an SOC2-type report if you have one.
- Escrow-like request: our procurement team asks for an assurance for business continuity — typical requests include source-code escrow or a similar release trigger. We understand that source-code escrow is sensitive; please propose alternatives (signed attestation + exportable, encrypted configuration backup?)

Attached: ACME_Redlines_MSA_v2.pdf and OrderForm_ACME_20260615.docx. Can you route this to your legal and ops teams and propose meeting times this week?

Appreciate your help — we are targeting a signing window by end of month.

Best,
Sarah Jenkins
Senior Counsel, ACME Corp

Hi Sarah — thanks for the detailed redlines and the timeline. Looping in Monica (Sales Ops) and Lauren (Solutions / deployment lead). I've also short-circuited Legal to start drafting a proposed addendum.

Quick answers to the bullets while Legal prepares formal language:

- License scope: Redwood's standard Order Form grants a production deployment license tied to the customer account and specific model artifact. For on-prem/VPC, we normally add an addendum that clarifies the license is limited to your infra and non-transferable without written permission; we can add language to permit DR/testing instances within agreed node counts or regions.
- Deployment rights: we are OK to permit DR instances and pre-production clusters; we typically include an upper bound on concurrent nodes and require notification if you exceed that. Please indicate targeted max nodes for production + DR so we can bake that into the addendum.
- Audit: Redwood can provide quarterly attestation covering operational controls and a SOC2 Type II report (we have one available for customers under NDA). Read-only log access into your VPC is not something we can provide from our hosted control plane; however, we can either: (a) provide a signed attestation + SOC2 report, or (b) support a scoped, on-site audit if required by procurement (costs/time to be covered by customer).
- Escrow: we understand code escrow is usually a non-starter for platform vendors. Our proposed alternatives: encrypted configuration + operational runbooks + a signed continuity attestation; for particularly sensitive sectors we also support a limited-scope binary escrow with strict release triggers negotiated in the addendum.

I've attached a short draft addendum (Proposed_OnPrem_Addendum_KI_20260616.pdf) with placeholders for node limits and the preferred audit option. Can we set up a 30-minute call tomorrow at 11am PT to go through the tradeoffs? If that doesn't work, Lauren suggested Thu 9am PT.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Karthik / Sarah — thanks for looping me in. I've reviewed ACME's redlines and Karthik's draft addendum. Below are Redwood's proposed positions and some alternative wording to keep negotiation moving: 

1) License scope / deployment rights
- Position: Grant a limited, non-exclusive license to use the Redwood runtime and model artifacts inside ACME-owned infrastructure (VPC or on-prem) for the Term, with the right to run separate DR and staging instances not to exceed a defined node count.
- Suggested clause: "Customer may deploy the Software and associated Model Artifacts within Customer-controlled environments (including VPCs and on-premises clusters) for Customer internal business purposes. DR and non-production clusters are permitted up to [X] nodes; Customer will notify Redwood if it intends to exceed this amount for a period longer than 14 days."

2) Audit / evidence requests
- Position: We will provide a current SOC2 Type II report under NDA and an annual attestation. We will not provide direct access to Redwood-managed production logs for on-prem customers. For audits requiring access beyond the SOC2 report, we propose a scoped tabletop or remote interview with our security team.
- Suggested compromise clause: "Upon reasonable notice and subject to confidentiality obligations, Redwood shall provide (i) a SOC2 Type II report covering the relevant controls, and (ii) a mutually agreed, scoped audit or attestation process. Any on-site audit requiring access to Redwood-managed systems shall be subject to reasonable timing and cost recovery by Redwood."

3) Escrow and continuity
- Position: We will not agree to unconditional source-code escrow. We can offer: (a) a repository snapshot of the runtime binaries and a key escrow for configuration artifacts held with a neutral third party, released only upon proof of Redwood insolvency or material breach; or (b) a documented Continuity Kit (runbooks, exported configs, authenticated backups) plus a signed continuity attestation.
- Suggested redline: "In lieu of source-code escrow, Redwood shall (i) deposit with a mutually agreed third party a binary snapshot and encrypted configuration artifacts subject to escrow release triggers defined herein, and (ii) furnish a Continuity Kit to Customer on execution of the Order Form."

4) Operational limits / support SLA impact
- Note: Allowing unlimited DR instances impacts cost/SLA. We propose a baseline node cap and an overage pricing schedule. We'll put numbers in the addendum once ACME confirms expected peak and DR counts.

Next steps: if ACME is comfortable with the escrow substitute language and the SOC2+attestation route, we can convert the draft PDF to redline and return by end of day tomorrow. Otherwise, happy to take these items to a short call.

--
Priyom Das
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Security & Legal

Thanks Priyom — this is helpful and aligns with what our procurement expects. A few clarifying items before we proceed to redline: 

- Node counts: ACME plans for 12 production GPU nodes and 6 DR nodes initially; staging will have 2 small nodes. Please confirm whether Redwood's cap would be set at 20 nodes total or whether production and DR are counted separately.
- Escrow triggers: the proposed binary snapshot + config escrow looks reasonable; procurement will want the release triggers spelled out (insolvency, failure to remedy material breach within 90 days, or prolonged unavailability exceeding X days). Can Redwood propose specific language for the triggers?
- SOC2 access: we will execute an NDA to receive the SOC2 Type II report. Please send the NDA and SOC2 intake instructions.

We're generally okay to proceed with the attestation + binary escrow approach and would like a redline of the addendum reflecting the suggested node caps and the audit choices. If you can send that by EOD tomorrow we can review and aim to sign the Order Form the following week.
